hook: Ray Kurzweil is an American inventor, computer scientist, and author known both for his technical contributions to pattern recognition technology and for his predictions about the future of artificial intelligence. Born in Queens, New York in 1948 and trained in computer science and literature at MIT, he began founding technology companies in 1973 and in 1976 introduced the Kurzweil Reading Machine, the first device able to convert printed text into spoken words for blind and visually impaired users. He went on to develop optical character recognition software able to read text in any typeface, along with early text to speech and speech recognition systems, work recognized with the National Medal of Technology and Innovation in 1999 and induction into the National Inventors Hall of Fame in 2002. Alongside his inventing career, Kurzweil became a widely read futurist, publishing books including The Age of Spiritual Machines and The Singularity Is Near that argue technological change is accelerating toward a point where machine intelligence will exceed human intelligence. In 2012 he joined Google, where he now holds the title of principal researcher and AI visionary, leading a team working on natural language understanding.

quick_facts: Born February 12, 1948, in Queens, New York
Invented the Kurzweil Reading Machine, the first print to speech device for the blind, in 1976
Received the National Medal of Technology and Innovation in 1999
Inducted into the National Inventors Hall of Fame in 2002
Holds the title of Principal Researcher and AI Visionary at Google
